subject: POC load signatures and acceptance plan
messages:
From: Erik Sørensen <erik@gridly.dev>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Trial load signatures & POC acceptance criteria

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment. Following up with a short recap and the things we need from Redwood to get the trial (POC) spun up. High-level goal: validate that Redwood can serve our live inference workload with acceptable latency/cost while handling our bursty end-of-period traffic.

Quick recap / asks from Gridly:
- Primary workload: real-time summarization + entity extraction for customer transcripts.
- Typical request size: ~120 tokens average (we'll send a CSV sample attached). Peak requests include hourly batching jobs that spike traffic.
- Target success metrics: p95 latency under 350ms for single-turn requests, error rate < 1% (5xx + timeouts), and throughput to sustain 60 RPS steady state. Cost sensitivity: need a rough per-1M-token cost estimate for the configuration you propose.

POC constraints we discussed:
- Duration: 2 weeks of traffic run (we'd like to start baseline testing week of May 24).
- Ownership: Gridly infra will provide sample payloads and auth tokens; Redwood to provide a staging endpoint + ingestion guidance.
- Data retention / privacy: responses will include PII — need to confirm retention and KMS approach for the POC.

Attachments: traffic_sample.csv (sample payloads, 1k rows)

Open items for Redwood: can you provide a proposed traffic matrix (RPS, concurrency, token distribution), a short acceptance checklist, and a kickoff date/time?

Cheers,
Erik
Head of Platform Engineering
Gridly
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Erik Sørensen <erik@gridly.dev>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial load signatures & POC acceptance criteria

Thanks Erik — great to sync. Drafting an initial intake below and flagging a couple clarifying Qs so we size the POC correctly.

PROPOSED TRIAL TRAFFIC MATRIX (baseline -> max):
- Sustained RPS (steady state): 60 RPS (client-provided baseline)
- Typical tokens/request: 120 tokens (you noted ~120) -> confirm average versus median
- Max tokens/request (worst-case): 2,048 tokens (if you have a tighter max pls advise)
- Concurrent open requests (client concurrency): 20 parallel streams
- Short bursts: up to 600 RPS for ~60–90s at hourly boundaries (batching windows)
- Long spikes: rare, up to 1,200 RPS for <15s (unlikely but observed during releases)

SUGGESTED SERVICE TARGETS (initial acceptance gates):
- Latency (p95): < 350ms for requests <= 512 tokens; p95 < 700ms for requests > 512 tokens
- Error rate (5xx/timeouts): < 1% measured over 1-hour windows
- Throughput: sustain 60 RPS for 2 hours with <1% errors
- Cost: provide per-1M-token estimate for the chosen model/quantization profile

CLARIFYING QUESTIONS:
1) Are you able to remove or redact PII in the CSV sample, or do we need to treat sample rows as production data? (affects retention / KMS)
2) Does your client use request-level caching or prefix caching now? If yes, can you share expected cache hit rates?
3) How tolerant is Gridly to tail latency outliers during bursts? Is missing 1–2 brief windows acceptable?

OWNERSHIP / NEXT STEPS:
- Redwood (Laura Bennett): provide validation harness + a test endpoint (deliver by Thu 21 May)
- Redwood (Aisha): finalize acceptance checklist + cost estimate (by Fri 22 May)
- Gridly (Erik): confirm token distribution and sanitize sample data (by Tue 20 May)
- Sales (Aditya): finalize trial contract terms and any credits (ongoing)

PROPOSED KICKOFF: May 26, 09:00 PT — 30m kickoff to confirm ingest/playbook and auth.

I'll attach an initial acceptance document after I incorporate answers to the clarifying Qs.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Trial load signatures & POC acceptance criteria

Thanks Aisha — quick updates after I ran the sample through our staging pipeline: a couple points:
- My earlier "typical tokens" callout should be average = 120 tokens, but median is closer to 90 tokens. Please use average=120, median=90 in the matrix.
- Bursts: hourly batch windows are the main spike source — we see ~600 RPS for 60s at the top of the hour, not 15s; rare multi-minute spikes up to 900 RPS during heavy report generation.
- We will not be able to fully redact PII in the sample; we can pseudonymize identifiers but will still need POC data protections (confirm KMS / retention).

Question for Redwood: do you have a recommended model size / quantization profile for this mix (latency-sensitive, ~120 avg tokens)? Also confirm whether prefix-level KV caching is possible in the short POC window (helps cut tokens and cost).

Erik
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Erik Sørensen <erik@gridly.dev>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial load signatures & POC acceptance criteria

Erik — appreciated, this helps tighten the plan. Updated intake notes below and confirmed owners / deliverables.

UPDATED TRAFFIC MATRIX (final for kickoff):
- Sustained RPS: 60 RPS
- Average tokens/request: 120 (median 90)
- Max tokens: 2048 (but <1% of calls)
- Concurrency: 20 parallel client streams
- Hourly bursts: 600 RPS for ~60–90s; occasional heavier bursts up to 900 RPS for <3 minutes

ACCEPTANCE CHECKPOINTS WE'LL RUN DURING THE POC:
- Baseline run (Day 1): validate connectivity, auth, sample requests -> target p95 < 350ms for requests <=512 tokens
- Stability run (Day 3–5): run sustained 60 RPS for 2 hours -> error rate < 1%
- Burst test (Day 6): simulate three hourly bursts at 600 RPS for 90s, measure tail latency and error rate (goal: p95 within target, graceful degradation under heavier bursts)
- Cost readout (end of trial): Redwood to provide per-1M-token and per-hour cost estimate for used config

OWNERSHIP & DELIVERABLES:
- Laura (Redwood): provide validation harness + CloudWatch/metric hooks + test endpoint by Thu 21 May
- Aisha (Redwood): final acceptance criteria doc (attached: poc-acceptance-criteria.pdf) and quick runbook for the ingestion script by Fri 22 May
- Aditya (Sales): finalize trial agreement & credits before kickoff
- Erik (Gridly): sanitize/pseudonymize sample data and provide a short runbook for client-side concurrency control by Tue 20 May

KICKOFF: Confirming May 26, 09:00 PT. I'll send a calendar invite.

If those items look good I'll mark this thread as the canonical intake and start tracking the checklist in the shared spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/EXAMPLE-TRAFFIC-MATRIX

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
